options_evaluated: Co-molded plastic with elastomer grip overmolds
assessments.rationale: A monomaterial polymer housing (such as pure ABS or PC) maximizes the ease and quality of recycling (parameter (d)) and ensures the avoidance of technical solutions detrimental to recycling (parameter (e), Page 79). Co-molded elastomer grips or composite fiberglass-reinforced plastics contaminate the recycling stream, which increases the amounts of waste generated in end-of-life treatment (parameter (r), Page 80) and increases the environmental footprint of EOL material recovery (parameter (m), Page 33, Page 80). Furthermore, avoiding composite polymers reduces the risk of microplastic and nanoplastic release during EOL shredding (parameter (p), Page 80).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Conflicts with the Manufacturing and Use-phase stages, as co-molded elastomer grips improve user ergonomics and slip resistance, while composite plastics offer higher impact durability and structural strength.

assessments.rationale: Threaded fasteners allow for non-destructive disassembly and re-assembly, which directly supports the ease of upgrading, reuse, remanufacturing, and refurbishment (parameter (c), Page 27, Page 79). This choice avoids technical solutions detrimental to EOL circular pathways (parameter (e), Page 79) like ultrasonic welding or permanent adhesives, which cause irreversible material damage during disassembly, thereby increasing the amounts of waste generated (parameter (r), Page 80) and the energy consumed in EOL treatment processes (parameter (g), Page 79).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Conflicts with the Manufacturing stage, as threaded fasteners increase the overall bill of materials, require longer assembly times, and raise production costs compared to ultrasonic welding or snap-fits.

options_evaluated: Brushless DC motor with modular/replaceable carbon-free assembly
Brushed DC motor with integrated/non-replaceable brushes
assessments.recommendation: Brushless DC motor with modular/replaceable carbon-free assembly
assessments.rationale: A modular, carbon-free brushless DC motor facilitates the ease of upgrading, reuse, remanufacturing, and refurbishment (parameter (c), Page 27, Page 79). It avoids solutions detrimental to circularity (parameter (e), Page 79) because brushed motors generate carbon dust and wear out permanently, leading to premature disposal and increased waste generation (parameter (r), Page 80). A modular brushless motor can be easily harvested, tested, and remanufactured (Page 27) to extend the product's lifecycle.
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Conflicts with the Manufacturing stage due to the higher initial cost of brushless motors and the added electronic complexity of the required motor controller.

options_evaluated: Passive cooling via open vents and heat sinks
Active cooling with a miniature fan
Phase-change materials (PCM) or thermal potting compounds
assessments.recommendation: Passive cooling via open vents and heat sinks
assessments.rationale: Passive cooling avoids technical solutions detrimental to recycling or recovery (parameter (e), Page 79). Thermal potting compounds or phase-change materials (PCMs) coat and contaminate internal electronics and plastics, which severely degrades the ease and quality of recycling (parameter (d)) and increases both the environmental footprint (parameter (m), Page 33, Page 80) and the amounts of waste generated in end-of-life treatment (parameter (r), Page 80) due to unrecyclable composite mixtures.
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Conflicts with the Use-phase stage, as open cooling vents reduce the tool's ingress protection (IP rating) against dust and moisture, and potting compounds provide superior shock absorption and heat dissipation under heavy loads.

assessments.rationale: A fully modular architecture with separate, easily detachable modules (battery, motor, switch, and gearbox) directly enhances the ease of upgrading, reuse, remanufacturing, and refurbishment (parameter (c), Page 27, Page 79). It avoids solutions detrimental to circularity (parameter (e), Page 79) and minimizes the amounts of waste generated in end-of-life treatment (parameter (r), Page 80) by allowing individual faulty modules to be repaired, refurbished, or replaced, rather than discarding the entire tool.
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Conflicts with the Design and Manufacturing stages, as a fully modular layout increases the physical size, weight, and internal wiring/connector complexity of the screwdriver, which may increase the initial material footprint.

options_evaluated: Removable and standardized slide-on Li-ion battery pack
assessments.recommendation: Removable and standardized slide-on Li-ion battery pack
assessments.rationale: A removable, standardized battery pack is critical for the ease of upgrading, reuse, remanufacturing, and refurbishment (parameter (c), Page 27, Page 79). It avoids solutions detrimental to recycling (parameter (e), Page 79); integrated or potted batteries represent hazardous waste that is difficult to extract, increasing safety risks and the energy/resources consumed in EOL treatment (parameter (g), Page 79). Standardized packs facilitate high-quality battery recycling and reuse in secondary applications, minimizing hazardous waste (parameter (r), Page 80).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Conflicts with the Design and Use-phase stages, as a standardized slide-on battery pack makes the screwdriver bulkier, heavier, and less compact than one with an integrated internal cell, and conflicts with Corded AC power which has infinite runtime but lacks portability.
